name: Accept a Next pager whose label carries a chevron glyph
request: Accept a Next pager whose label carries a chevron glyph
checks: npm run check passed end to end: typecheck, build, 423/423 tests (up from 422, one added), validate (31 build files, 4 React entry points, service-worker imports)

behaviour spot-checked directly: Next, 'Next >', 'Next arrow', bare chevrons, Next page, Show more, Load more and Page 2 are allowed; bare 2/3/10 refused; Next: Message, Message Next, 'Next > Reject', Save and Shortlist all refused as forbidden-action; a bare chevron with inContainer false refused as outside-applicant-list
click budget unchanged at exactly seven; no new control and no new call site - only the label the existing pagination control is matched by
the one pre-existing assertion pinning the old literal was updated deliberately and records why; rule 9h amended in the same task to describe the stripping and its limits
NOT verified against live LinkedIn (rule 17): the label was read from the user's screenshot, not from a live run, and whether pressing it actually advances the list is still unproven
result: The live pager on the recruiter's 665-applicant job renders 'Next >' with a chevron glyph, and textContent includes it. APPLICANT_PAGINATION_PATTERN is anchored on the whole label - deliberately, so 'Next: Message' can never match - so 'next >' was refused as not-a-pagination-control and the run never left page one. That is worse than merely stopping: with no pager found the walk reports settled, which isConclusiveListStop treats as a real end of list, so the job was marked COMPLETED at roughly 25 of 665 and the reload-resume was disabled with it. Added paginationLabel(), which strips chevron and arrow glyphs before the allowlist is applied, and treats a control whose whole name is the glyph as 'next'. Stripping rather than widening the pattern keeps the anchor meaningful - removing a glyph from 'Next: Message' leaves 'next: message', which still fails - and the denylist is still consulted first. Numbered page buttons stay refused on purpose, since a bare 2 would make any numeric control in the list a pager.
